title: Microsoft Tech Support Scam - Time to end this.
description: Special thanks to all the techies who scammed the scammers. Some of these videos are hilarious. Can't believe the language though... WOW! Join our Indigogo Campaign "Damn The Scam" to increase public awareness about these terrible criminal scams.  Computers can be intimidating. But they really shouldn't be. Computer repair can be very expensive. But it doesn't have to be. Honest local computer businesses all over the world are losing millions of dollars in revenue to Indian telemarketers who are cold calling innocent people, telling them there is a virus on their computer.  Even a search for “technical support” on Microsoft's own search engine brings up these phony foreign companies pretending to be affiliated with Microsoft. And their scams are very similar. Now, we're not against anyone making an honest living. But this is a pure scam. It's criminal. Most of these companies are offshore, and who knows what kind of terrorist activities your money is funding. They're preying on the fear of good people all over the world. What most people don't realize is this is a complete scam. Indian scammers laugh at honest European and American citizens, calling us “naïve, ignorant, and stupid.” Many of my customers have fallen for this scam. And they're not dumb people. We're talking former CEOs, attorneys, doctors, and engineers. There have been several cases of these scammers threatening good, hardworking people. We've called the local newspapers and television stations several times. I've posted this on social media at least a hundred times. Still, I cannot get anyone to report on these Indian telemarketing scammers. So I'm asking for your help. In addition to my computer business, I run a small marketing agency. And what we want to do is buy ads to let innocent people know about this scam.  We want to place paid advertising on social media, in magazines, and on television. But we need your help. This trickery needs to end. Thanks for watching. Please like, subscribe, and share.  How telemarketers get around the Do Not Call list: http://www.cbsnews.com/news/how-telemarketers-get-around-the-do-not-call-list/  Thanks to all the other techs who took the time to expose these criminals. textual.limitations: The records do not verify the callers' identities, the search results, or whether any specific company was affiliated or unaffiliated with Microsoft.

applications and the harmful links which are running in your computer,. Which is not safe for your computer,
